Shopify Website for Digital Product Sellers: A Practical Guide

By Marie Glow StudioUpdated September 23, 2026

Digital products have an odd problem on a store page: the buyer cannot see, hold or test the thing before paying. Planners, templates, printables, guides and courses all rely on the page to do the convincing. A Shopify website for digital products therefore has to answer questions a physical store never gets asked, such as "What file will I receive?", "Can I use this for my business?" and "What if it does not open?"

This guide walks through the pieces that matter most, in the order a buyer runs into them. If you are still deciding whether digital is the right lane at all, the physical versus digital products post compares the two.

Show what is inside before anyone pays

A buyer decides in seconds whether a digital product looks useful. Give them enough to judge without giving the product away.

Previews

Show a few real pages, screens or sample sections. For a planner, that might be two or three spreads. For a template, a look at the layout and the editable areas. For a guide, the contents page and one sample page. Make the preview images large enough to read.

Mockups

A mockup places your product in context: the printable on a desk, the template on a laptop screen. Mockups help the buyer picture using it, but they should never show things that are not in the download. If the mockup includes a frame or a plant, say the frame and plant are not included.

A plain list of what is in the file

List the number of pages or files, the format (PDF, editable file, image set), the size or dimensions, and which software opens it. This one list prevents most confused emails.

Set delivery expectations on the page

Buyers of digital products expect to get the file quickly, and they worry when they do not know how. Say it before checkout, in a short block near the buy button: how the file arrives (an email, a download link, a page in their account), that they should check their spam folder, and what to do if the link fails. Keep the wording honest to how your store is actually set up. If you tell people a file arrives instantly, test a real purchase yourself first.

The Complete Website and Brand Identity covers full Shopify setup and product organization for up to 20 items. How a particular download delivery method is configured is worth confirming with Marie Glow Studio at hello@marieglowstudio.com before you buy.

Make licensing and refunds impossible to miss

Two things create the most friction for digital sellers, and both are fixable with clear words.

Licensing

State what the buyer may do: personal use, use in their own business, or resale. State what they may not do, such as sharing the file, reselling it as is or claiming it as their own. Put a short version on the product page and a full version on a dedicated page. Keep it in plain language and have a professional review it if it matters to your business.

Refunds

Once a file is downloaded, it cannot be returned, so many digital sellers do not offer refunds on delivered files. Whatever your policy is, put it on the product page and in your policy pages, not only in the footer. Spelling it out reduces disputes, and the brand trust guide explains why clear policies build confidence.

Turn buyers and browsers into subscribers

Digital products are a natural fit for an email list. A free sample, a mini version of the product or a short checklist gives visitors a reason to sign up, and an email list lets you tell them about the next release without paying for traffic again. Lead magnet ideas for product-based businesses and Pinterest and email marketing are good next reads.

Use Pinterest to bring people in

Pinterest suits digital products because people search there for planners, printables, templates and ideas, and pins can keep surfacing for months. Pin the preview and the mockup images, write keyword-aware titles and descriptions, and send each pin to the specific product page, not the homepage. The full approach is in Pinterest marketing for digital products. No one can guarantee traffic or sales, and results take weeks or months of consistent effort. If you also coach or teach, the one page website guide for coaches covers a lighter option for that side.

Frequently asked questions

What should a digital product page on Shopify include?

A digital product page should show large previews and a mockup, a plain list of what is in the file (pages, format and compatible software), the price, how and when the file is delivered, licensing terms and the refund policy. This answers the questions a buyer cannot test in person.

How do I explain licensing for digital products?

State in plain language what the buyer may do, such as personal use or use in their own business, and what they may not do, such as sharing or reselling the file. Put a short version on the product page and the full terms on a linked policy page.

Should digital products have a refund policy?

That is your decision, but the policy must be visible. Some sellers do not offer refunds on delivered files because a download cannot be returned. Whatever you choose, state it on the product page and in your policy pages so buyers know before they pay.

Can Pinterest drive traffic to a digital product store?

It can. Pinterest works as a visual search engine where people look for planners, printables and templates, and pins can keep surfacing for months. It takes clear product pages, keyword-aware pins and steady effort, and results are never guaranteed.
